name: Plain Mouse
lede: Plain Mouse is ColorHub's English name for Su-nezumi, the baseline grey of a Japanese family of named "mouse" colors that range from near-white to near-black.

sections.title: The mouse family's middle grade
sections.body:
Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors gives this swatch as Su-nezumi (素鼠), where su means "plain" or "undyed" and nezumi ("mouse") marks the family of muted greys it heads [1]. Unlike [[pale-taupe|Gin-nezumi]] ("silver mouse") or other graded members of the same family, Su-nezumi names the baseline, unmodified grey before any lightening or darkening word is added [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 places it in block 64, "brownish gray," about 5.5 units from that block's centre [2]. The library's nearest other named colors, [[mole-brown]] and [[mole-brown]], are each 2.7 units away [2].

Measured in LCH it reads lightness 42, chroma 8, hue 56 degrees, a mid-toned, warm-leaning grey [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 1,796 of 23,781 paintings, about 8 percent, as photographed [3]. It plays a mid-tone role most often, 53 percent of its occurrences, with shadow and highlight splitting the rest [3]. Theodor Philipsen and the Norwegian painter Johan Christian Dahl each carry it at more than four times the archive's overall rate [3]. It shares canvases more than chance with the color word Silver, and its presence peaks around the 1270s [3].
